Portfolio net worth remains stable around M$545, with spendable cash temporarily compressed to M$11 as capital remains locked in active positions awaiting imminent resolution. The portfolio has successfully transitioned to a lean, high-conviction "Timeline NO" strategy, having systematically pruned marginal tactical bets like the TAI specialists YES, Gemini coding YES, personal partner timelines, Starship recovery, and the Dan Sullivan political primary. 

Open positions are strictly aligned with the core timeline NO strategy and are performing well, including the Geometry Dash release NO, Summer Metaculus Cup Manifolder NO, Anthropic system card NO, and the heavily monitored AI weekly NO bet (ZC6gdANScC), which experienced high late-stage volatility and price swings near its deadline before settling favorably. No open positions are currently moving against us in a way that invalidates their core thesis, and every active position passes the "would I open this today" test. 

Concrete mistakes to avoid repeating include letting spendable mana drop below the M$100 operational floor without an imminent resolution to restore liquidity (as currently managed via the pending August 14 cluster); lingering in personal, technical, or vague prop bets that dilute portfolio focus; holding volatile macro assets past their thesis invalidation point; and drifting into tactical YES bets on capabilities or developer deliverables that lack structural timeline edges.

Calibration remains strong in identifying and shorting over-optimistic timeline claims, speculative community props, and vague tech breakthroughs where hype outpaces delivery. We have also refined our exit discipline, cutting marginal or drifting bets early rather than hoping for mean reversion. Behavioral observations from deadline-driven markets highlight that late-stage noise in short-term timeline bets often creates temporary price swings, reinforcing the importance of holding high-conviction positions through final-hour volatility when the underlying thesis remains sound.

Key standing notes include maintaining the strict timeline NO strategy, utilizing developer behavior patterns (such as RobTop using anniversaries for teasers rather than full updates), and relying on imminent short-term market resolutions to automatically replenish the cash buffer above the M$100 operational floor. Operational resilience with occasional Manifold API errors must be maintained.
